subject: Visualization of interaction between fixed effects

messages.author: fd5b3eee58ac5e83
messages.subject: Visualization of interaction between fixed effects
parts:
Good evening.

I included a few fixed effect interactions in my spatio-temporal Bayesian model (BYM model formulation similar to the example in Blangiardo et al.). I want to make a plot so that one can better understand the coefficients for the interactions.

For a simple GLM, I would usually fit the model, create a dataset with everything set to the mean except for the 2 variables I want to visualize the interaction for, and then predict on that dataset to obtain results for each of the values for the 2 variables.

How can I do something similar for the INLA model? I do not have an interaction between space and time, i.e. my fixed effect interaction is the same for each point in space and time.

messages.author: 74f2e6fef4c447fd
messages.subject: Re: Visualization of interaction between fixed effects
parts:
Hi Brigitte,

You can follow the same process, except creating the predictions is a bit more involved. 

As far as I understand, your model is a GLMM, with zero-centered, spatially and temporally structured random effects. To explore fixed effects behavior, you can ignore the random effects and make predictions based on the fixed effect estimates. You make a prediction dataset like before. You get fixed effect estimates using inla.posterior.sample().

Below is an example with a simpler GLMM, with only a random intercept. Maybe you can adapt this code to your example.

Best,
Tim

----------

# load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(INLA)

# helper function to get samples from fixed effect posteriors
get_fixed_samples <- function(mod=r1, ss=10) {
  fe <- c(rownames(mod$summary.fixed))
  idx <- as.list(rep(0, length(fe)))
  names(idx) <- fe
  samp <- inla.posterior.sample(n=ss, result=mod, selection=idx)
  samp <- t(as.data.frame(lapply(samp, function(x) x$latent)))
  samp <- as.matrix(as.data.frame(samp))
  colnames(samp) <- fe
  rownames(samp) <- NULL
  return(samp)
}

# make data with random intercept and two interacting continuous fixed effects
ngroups <- 10
nobs <- 100
beta0 <- 5
beta1 <- 1
beta2 <- 2
beta3 <- -3
dat <- data.frame(x1 = runif(nobs, -1, 1),
                   x2 = runif(nobs, -1, 1),
                   mygroup = rep(seq_len(ngroups), nobs / ngroups)) %>%
  mutate(y = beta0 + 
           (beta1 * x1) + 
           (beta2 * x2) + 
           (beta3 * x1 * x2) + 
           (rnorm(ngroups)[mygroup]) +
           rnorm(nobs, sd = 0.1),
         x2_cat=factor(cut(x2, breaks = 5)))
summary(dat)

# plot it to see interaction in generated data
ggplot(dat, aes(x1, y, group=mygroup)) + geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method="lm", se=F) + facet_wrap(~x2_cat)

# run inla model and specify config=T for posterior sampling
form1 <- y ~ 1 + x1 * x2 + f(mygroup, model="iid")
res1 <- inla(form1, data = as.data.frame(dat),
             control.compute=list(config=T))
summary(res1) # looks like mean param estimates match input values

# get samples from fixed effect posteriors
nsim <- 1000
samps <- get_fixed_samples(mod=res1, ss=nsim)

# make prediction covariate matrix that has same columns as sample matrix
newdat <- expand.grid(`(Intercept)`=1, 
                      x1=seq(-1, 1, length.out=20),
                      x2=seq(-1, 1, length.out=20)) %>%
  mutate(`x1:x2`=x1 * x2) %>% as.matrix()
head(samps)
head(newdat)

# make matrix for the predictions and fill it
fitmat <- matrix(nrow=nrow(newdat), ncol=nsim)
for(i in 1:nsim) fitmat[,i] <- newdat %*% samps[i,]

# summarize prediction matrix
preds <- as.data.frame(newdat) %>% 
  mutate(mean=apply(fitmat, 1, mean),
        lcl=apply(fitmat, 1, quantile, prob=0.025),
        ucl=apply(fitmat, 1, quantile, prob=0.975),
        x2_cat=factor(cut(x2, breaks = 5))) %>%
  arrange(x1)

# plot predictions that demonstrate interaction between fixed effects
ggplot(preds %>% group_by(x1,x2_cat) %>% sample_n(1)) + 
  geom_linerange(aes(x=x1, ymin=lcl, ymax=ucl, color=x2_cat), alpha=0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(x=x1, y=mean, color=x2_cat), alpha=0.8) # + 
  # facet_wrap(~x2_cat) 
ggplot(preds, aes(x=x1, y=x2, z=mean)) + geom_contour_filled()

# make an interactive version of the interaction (best viewed in RStudio)
plot_ly() %>% add_surface(x=~unique(preds$x1), y=~unique(preds$x2), 
                          z=matrix(preds$mean, nrow=length(unique(preds$x2))))
